newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electric futures end higher, erases loss.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electric futures end higher, erases loss.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures delivered at the California-Oregon Border (COB) finished higher Friday, erasing early losses as daily physical prices stablized in late trading.
"Physical prices are trading slightly higher than the screen," a Northwest trader said. Monday prices for COB power were quoted at $23.00-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
The entire complex was pressured since mid-week by outlook of very mild weather, softer natural gas prices and ample hydro and nuclear generation in the western U.S.
December COB futures settled at $23.58, up 13 cents after hitting a session low of $22.35.
January 1997 COB erased a 81 cent loss finished at $20.89, up 33 cents. February COB ended down 35 cents at $17.45.
December PV futures settled at 28 cents at $21.75, trimming a 58 cent loss.
January 1997 PV finished up 13 cents at $19.50 after reaching a session low of $18.50. February PV ended up 35 cents at $18.00.
A 428 megawatt (MW) unit at the Craig generating station in Colorado was scheduled to shut late today until Monday for maintenance.
The 720 MW unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired generating station near Page, Ariz., was set to be idled until December for seasonal maintenance.
Some brokers and traders expected the complex to stablize after recent volatility.
"It'll probably going to go sideway. We had three, four pretty volatile weeks," the Northwest trader said.
